how_customers_find_and_choose: Households and shops find service providers through neighbours, the map listing and shared contact in chat groups
Business and industrial clients choose contractors on safety record, past projects and responsiveness
Customers want a quick response time for faults: first reply fast, a visit time and a clear price estimate
For recurring supply such as water or waste collection, reliability and punctuality are the main reasons customers stay
what_works_now: A clear schedule of visits or deliveries shared with each customer in chat
A quick reply to fault calls with a name, an arrival time and a short explanation of what will be done
Written estimates and completion notes with before and after photos
A record of each customer's address, equipment and past service for faster visits
A reminder to regular customers when a service, filter change or refill is due, with consent
A complete map listing with service area, hours and contact
Basic safety information shared plainly with customers
outdated_or_weak: Quoting a fixed price without seeing the site or fault
Missing a promised time with no message
Handbills and wall chalking as the main way to be found
Ignoring the safety record in favour of the lowest bid
Generic digital marketing advice without a service area or schedule behind it

PK: Cash on delivery and cash at the counter are still common; bank transfer and mobile wallet payments are now normal for many customers
Ramadan and the two Eids reshape demand, opening hours and staff availability every year
Summer heat, monsoon rain and power cuts affect operations and footfall
Customers often write in Urdu, Roman Urdu or a regional language, and chat is the usual first contact
Load shedding and power cuts drive demand for backup power; summer peak shapes workload
Utility and fuel rules are set by the regulators; the owner confirms specifics with them
Water supply problems drive demand for tankers and filters in many areas
UAE: Customers are multilingual and expect quick replies in chat; card and tap payments are normal
Winter is the busy season; many residents travel in summer so demand can dip
Ramadan and Eid change hours and buying patterns; the licence a business holds decides what it may sell and advertise, so the owner checks that with the licensing body
Utility services are regulated by the authority; summer cooling load defines peak demand
Work in energy and industrial sites needs approvals and safety permits; the owner confirms specifics
CA: Customers expect online booking or enquiry, card and bank e-transfer payment, and clear written confirmation
Long winters and a short summer peak shape outdoor and seasonal trades
English and French (in Quebec) matter, and many communities prefer their own language; consent for marketing messages and sales tax rules vary, so the owner checks them with a professional
Electrical, gas and waste work needs licensed trades and permits by province; the owner confirms specifics with the authority
Winter outages and storms drive emergency work

never_assume: Service records in a tracked form
